title: How do we fill in these unit blanks?
description: Six decimal measures are changed from one unit to another. The video multiplies when the new unit is smaller, divides when it is bigger, and moves the decimal point by the number of zeros in ten, a hundred or a thousand.
teaching_notes: One idea: a smaller unit needs a bigger number, so multiply; a bigger unit needs a smaller number, so divide; and ten, a hundred or a thousand move the decimal point one, two or three places. Ask the class whether the number of metres should be bigger or smaller than the number of kilometres before any work is shown. Watch for students who multiply when they should divide.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q5
video_script.why: The child can divide a decimal by a whole number to get the amount for one, and now multiplies or divides by ten, a hundred or a thousand to change a unit.
video_script.substitution: A smaller unit means multiplying by the number of small units in one big unit, and a bigger unit means dividing by it, which moves the decimal point.
video_script.anchor: Six blanks to fill: 5.5 km = ___ m, 35 cm = ___ m, 14.5 cm = ___ mm, 68 g = ___ kg, 9.02 m = ___ mm, 125.5 ml = ___ l, with the unit facts beside them
video_script.payoff_line: Each blank is filled by multiplying or dividing by ten, a hundred or a thousand

final_answer.spoken: five thousand five hundred metres, zero point three five metres, one hundred forty five millimetres, zero point zero six eight kilograms, nine thousand twenty millimetres and zero point one two five five litres

video_script.design: One idea: a smaller unit means a bigger number, so multiply; a bigger unit means a smaller number, so divide. The unit facts stay on the board all video; the working band shows the six operations in two steps, then the decimal point rule, and the answers appear only in the answer beat.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the unit facts 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 g = 1000 mg, 1 l = 1000 ml; then six blanks: 5.5 km = ___ m, 35 cm = ___ m, 14.5 cm = ___ mm, 68 g = ___ kg, 9.02 m = ___ mm, 125.5 ml = ___ l

marks.length: the length facts 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 km = 1000 m appear
marks.weight: the weight and volume facts 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 g = 1000 mg, 1 l = 1000 ml appear
marks.blank1: the blanks 5.5 km = ___ m and 35 cm = ___ m appear
marks.blank2: the blanks 14.5 cm = ___ mm and 68 g = ___ kg appear
marks.blank3: the blanks 9.02 m = ___ mm and 125.5 ml = ___ l appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about changing units.
<bookmark mark='length'/>One centimetre is ten millimetres. One metre is one hundred centimetres. One kilometre is one thousand metres.
<bookmark mark='weight'/>One kilogram is one thousand grams. One gram is one thousand milligrams. One litre is one thousand millilitres.
<bookmark mark='blank1'/>Fill in the blanks. Five point five kilometres is how many metres? Thirty five centimetres is how many metres?
<bookmark mark='blank2'/>Fourteen point five centimetres is how many millimetres? Sixty eight grams is how many kilograms?
<bookmark mark='blank3'/>Nine point zero two metres is how many millimetres? One hundred twenty five point five millilitres is how many litres?

beats.on_screen: the unit facts and the six blanks hold still and get an accent underline; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a long stick cut into small bits: smaller unit, bigger number, multiply; bigger unit, smaller number, divide

marks.bits: a one metre stick is cut into small pieces and the pieces are counted
marks.mult: the words smaller unit, bigger number, multiply are written
marks.div: the words bigger unit, smaller number, divide are written

narration: <bookmark mark='bits'/>A stick measured in small units has many pieces. In a big unit, the same stick has few.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>When we change to a smaller unit, the number gets bigger, so we multiply.
<bookmark mark='div'/>When we change to a bigger unit, the number gets smaller, so we divide.

beats.on_screen: Given: the unit facts and the six measures 5.5 km, 35 cm, 14.5 cm, 68 g, 9.02 m, 125.5 ml

marks.given: the unit facts and the six measures are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the unit facts, and six measures to change into a new unit.

beats.on_screen: To find: each measure in the new unit

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find each measure in the new unit.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, to a smaller unit, multiply: 5.5 km to m: 5.5 × 1000; 14.5 cm to mm: 14.5 × 10; 9.02 m to mm: 1 m = 100 cm = 100 × 10 mm = 1000 mm, so 9.02 × 1000

marks.why: the step title and the three measures that go to a smaller unit are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step one, three measures go to a smaller unit, so we multiply.
<bookmark mark='km'/>Five point five kilometres: one kilometre is one thousand metres. Multiply five point five by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='cm'/>Fourteen point five centimetres: one centimetre is ten millimetres. Multiply fourteen point five by ten.
<bookmark mark='m'/>Nine point zero two metres: one metre is one hundred centimetres, and each centimetre is ten millimetres.
<bookmark mark='mm'/>That makes one metre one thousand millimetres, so we multiply by one thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, to a bigger unit, divide: 35 cm to m: 35 ÷ 100; 68 g to kg: 68 ÷ 1000; 125.5 ml to l: 125.5 ÷ 1000

marks.why: the step title and the three measures that go to a bigger unit are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='why'/>Step two, three measures go to a bigger unit, so we divide.
<bookmark mark='cm'/>Thirty five centimetres: one metre is one hundred centimetres. Divide thirty five by one hundred.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Sixty eight grams: one kilogram is one thousand grams. Divide sixty eight by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='ml'/>One hundred twenty five point five millilitres: one litre is one thousand millilitres. Divide by one thousand.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: × 10: point 1 place right; × 1000: point 3 places right; ÷ 100: point 2 places left; ÷ 1000: point 3 places left; empty places get zeros

marks.right: × 10 and × 1000 are written with arrows to the right of one place and three places
marks.left: ÷ 100 and ÷ 1000 are written with arrows to the left of two places and three places
marks.zero: a zero fills an empty place

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step three, multiplying moves the decimal point to the right. Ten moves it one place, and one thousand moves it three places.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Dividing moves the decimal point to the left. One hundred moves it two places, and one thousand moves it three places.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>We fill any empty place with a zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the size: a bigger unit gives a smaller number; a smaller unit gives a bigger number

marks.cmp: each result is compared with its starting number
marks.rule: the check words are written: bigger unit, smaller number; smaller unit, bigger number

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>Step four, check each result against the number we began with.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Going from kilometres to metres, the number must grow. Going from centimetres to metres, the number must shrink.

marks.ans: the six blanks are filled and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each blank is filled by multiplying or dividing by ten, a hundred or a thousand.
<bookmark mark='pair1'/>Five point five kilometres is five thousand five hundred metres. Thirty five centimetres is zero point three five metres.
<bookmark mark='pair2'/>Fourteen point five centimetres is one hundred forty five millimetres. Sixty eight grams is zero point zero six eight kilograms.
<bookmark mark='pair3'/>Nine point zero two metres is nine thousand twenty millimetres. One hundred twenty five point five millilitres is zero point one two five five litres.
